newsitem.title: GERMANY: German fire insurers expect high loss for 1996.
newsitem.headline: German fire insurers expect high loss for 1996.

text.p: German industrial fire insurers are likely to suffer "substantial underwriting losses of several hundred million marks" in 1996, according to a leading insurer.

Dankwart von Schultzendorff, board member of Colonia Versicherungs-AG, told Reuters that a soft market had led this year to a reduction in gross premium income by around 250 million marks ($166 million), from 4.2 million marks in 1995 to 3.95 million marks in 1996.
In 1997, a further reduction could be expected, "at least the level of that seen in 1996," Von Schultzendorff said.

"Even if we had this year the comparatively favourable loss situation of 1995, the market would have suffered an underwriting loss of 80 million marks, compared with a profit of 170 million marks in 1995," said von Schultzendorf.
"But unfortunately, the losses are about 15 percent or 480 million marks above the level of 1995."
Falling income and higher losses both contributed to the expected underwriting loss. In 1995, the loss ratio had been 76.7 percent, in 1996 it would exceed 90 percent, to which costs had to be added.

"The cycles in industrial insurance are getting shorter," said von Schultzendorff. "But at the same time, its mechanics are changing." There was a clear trend that solidarity in the insurance industry was declining.

Among the major losses suffered by German insurers in 1996 are the Duesseldorf airport fire of 11 April 1996, which is estimated by insurers to cost them in excess of 350 million marks. A fire at the Lingen plant of the chemical group Baerlocher on 16 June 1996 cost around 100 million marks. ($1=1.5021 Mark)
